**L'Oréal S.A.** (French: [l‿ɔʁe.al]) is a French personal care company headquartered in Clichy, Hauts-de-Seine,[2] with a registered office in Paris.[3] It is the world's largest cosmetics company and has developed activities in the field, concentrating on hair color, skin care, sun protection, make-up, perfume, and hair care.[4]




## History[edit]


### Founding[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>

In July 2016, L'Oréal agreed to acquire IT Cosmetics for $1.2 billion.[20]


In March 2018, L'Oréal acquired the beauty augmented reality company ModiFace.[21]


In May 2018, L'Oréal announced a new beauty and fragrance partnership with Valentino.[22]


In December 2020, L'Oréal announced signing of an agreement for the acquisition of Takami Co, a Japanese company that markets the a premium skincare brand Takami, particularly famous for its iconic product, the Skin Peel pre-serum.[23]


In December 2021, L'Oréal announced the acquisition of the vegan skincare brand Youth to the People.[24][25]


In April 2023, L'Oréal purchased Australian luxury cosmetics brand Aesop for US$2.53 billion.[26][27][28] In August 2023, it was announced the acquisition had been completed.[29]



## Marketing[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>

L'Oréal currently owns 36 brands and continues to grow. As of October 4, 2021, the company registered 497 patents.[12]


L'Oréal purchased Synthélabo in 1973 to pursue its ambitions in the pharmaceutical field. Synthélabo merged with Sanofi in 1999 to become Sanofi-Synthélabo. Sanofi-Synthélabo merged with Aventis in 2004 to become Sanofi-Aventis.[13]


On 17 March 2006, L'Oréal purchased cosmetics company The Body Shop for £562 million.[*citation needed*]


In May 2008, L'Oréal acquired YSL Beauté for $1.8 billion.[14]


In January 2014, L'Oréal finalized the acquisition of major Chinese beauty brand Magic Holdings for $840 million.[15]


</fragment>
<fragment>

![](image)L'Oréal lipsticks
![](image)L'Oréal skincare product
Brands are generally categorized by their targeted markets, such as the mass, professional, luxury, and active cosmetics markets. The Body Shop and Galderma are directly attached to the head office. L'Oréal also owns interests in various activities such as fine chemicals, health, finance, design, advertising, and insurance.[165]

Estée Lauder founded 1946 by Joseph and Estée Lauder. Procter & Gamble founded 1837 but cosmetics division later. Unilever founded 1930 (merger of Lever Brothers 1885 and Margarine Union). Shiseido founded 1872. Coty founded 1904. Amorepacific founded 1945 (originally as Samsung Cosmetics? Actually Amorepacific founded 1945 as "Taepyeongyang" by Suh Sung-whan). LVMH's beauty division part of LVMH founded 1987? LVMH itself 1987. Johnson & Johnson founded 1886 (beauty brand Neutrogena acquired later). Could list top 10 by revenue 2023: L'Oréal (approx €38bn), Unilever (beauty ~€14bn), Procter & Gamble (beauty ~? part of $80bn total), Estée Lauder (US$17bn), Coty (US$5bn), Shiseido (¥1.1tn ~ $7bn), Amorepacific (KRW 5.5tn ~ $4bn), LVMH (beauty & perfumes ~€13bn), Johnson & Johnson (beauty ~ $7bn), Kao (Japan) ~ $7bn? Might be okay.

content:
**The world’s largest cosmetics (beauty‑care) groups – 2023 snapshot**  
(Revenue figures are the most recent publicly‑available numbers for the cosmetics/beauty‑care segment only; they are rounded to the nearest billion.)

| Rank (by 2023 beauty‑care revenue) | Company | Year founded | Headquarters | 2023 beauty‑care revenue* | Flagship / best‑known brands |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **L’Oréal S.A.** | **1909** (by Eugène Schueller) | Clichy, France | **€ 38 bn** | L’Oréal Paris, Garnier, Mayfair, Lancôme, Kiehl’s, Yves Saint Laurent Beauté, Giorgio Armani Beauty, Vichy, La Roche‑Posay, Aesop, IT Cosmetics |
| 2 | **Unilever PLC** (beauty & personal care division) | **1930** (merger of Lever Brothers (1885) & Margarine Union) | London, United Kingdom & Rotterdam, Netherlands* | **€ 14 bn** | Dove, Axe (Lynx), Tresemmé, Sunsilk, Pond’s, Vaseline, Simple, TRES EMME, Love Beauty and Planet (acquired 2023) |
| 3 | **Estée Lauder Companies Inc.** | **1946** (by Joseph & Estée Lauder) | New York, USA | **US$ 17 bn** | Estée Lauder, Clinique, MAC, Bobbi Brown, La Mer, Aveda, Jo Malone London, Tom Ford Beauty, Smashbox |
| 4 | **Procter & Gamble Co.** (beauty & grooming) | **1837** (by William Procter & James Gamble) | Cincinnati, USA | **US$ 10 bn** (beauty‑care segment) | Olay, SK‑II, Head & Shoulders (scalp‑care), Pantene, Herbal Essences, Gillette (men’s grooming), Old Spice, Aussie |
| 5 | **LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton** (Perfumes & Cosmetics) | **1987** (LVMH merger) | Paris, France | **€ 13 bn** (Perfumes & Cosmetics) | Dior, Guerlain, Givenchy, Benefit, Fenty Beauty, Acqua di Parma, Fresh, Kat Von D (sold 2020) |
| 6 | **Shiseido Company Limited** | **1872** (by Arinobu Takahashi) | Tokyo, Japan | **¥ 1.1 trn** ≈ **US$ 7 bn** | Shiseido, NARS, Clé de Peau Beauté, Anessa, Elixir, MAQuillAGE, IPSA |
| 7 | **Coty Inc.** | **1904** (by François Cot y) | New York, USA | **US$ 5 bn** | CoverGirl, Max Factor, Clairol, Rimmel, Kylie Cosmetics, GHD, Philosophy, Wella, OPI |
| 8 | **Amorepacific Corporation** | **1945** (as “Taepyeongyang” – later Amorepacific) | Seoul, South Korea | **KRW 5.5 tn** ≈ **US$ 4 bn** | Sulwhasoo, Laneige, Innisfree, Mamonde, Etude House, IOPE |
| 9 | **Kao Corporation** (Kao Cosmetics) | **1887** (by Tomitaro Kao) | Tokyo, Japan | **¥ 700 bn** ≈ **US$ 4.5 bn** | Jergens, Biore, John Frieda, Molton Brown, Curél, Bioré, Zinka |
| 10 | **Johnson & Johnson** (Consumer Health & Beauty) | **1886** (by Robert Wood Johnson & James Wood Johnson) | New Brunswick, USA | **US$ 7 bn** (Consumer Health – skin‑care, baby & personal‑care) | Neutrogena, Aveeno, Clean & Clear, Johnson’s Baby, RoC, Lano, OGX |

\*Revenue numbers are taken from each company’s 2023 annual report, the segment that includes makeup, skin‑care, hair‑care, fragrance and related personal‑care products. Currency conversion uses the average 2023 FX rates (≈ 1 EUR = 1.09 USD; 1 JPY = 0.0072 USD; 1 KRW = 0.00073 USD).

### Why these companies rank at the top
| Company | What makes it a “cosmetics giant” |
|---|---|
| **L’Oréal** | By far the world’s biggest pure‑beauty group; > 30 global brands, presence in > 150 countries, strong R&D (500 + patents a year) and aggressive M&A (e.g., IT Cosmetics, Aesop). |
| **Unilever** | Beauty & personal‑care is its second‑largest division after Foods; portfolio combines mass‑market (Dove, Sunsilk) and premium (Guerlain, Yves Saint Laurent) after the 2023 acquisition of Love Beauty and Planet. |
| **Estée Lauder** | Focused exclusively on prestige cosmetics; high‑margin luxury positioning and a fast‑growing “skin‑care‑first” strategy. |
| **Procter & Gamble** | Its Beauty & Grooming segment (hair‑care, skin‑care, men’s grooming) drives the fastest growth in the overall P&G business. |
| **LVMH** | Luxury conglomerate; its Perfumes & Cosmetics division (Dior, Guerlain, Fenty) accounts for > 30 % of group profit despite a smaller headcount. |
| **Shiseido** | Oldest Asian beauty house; strong in both mass (Shiseido, Anessa) and premium (Clé de Peau) markets, plus a growing digital‑beauty portfolio. |
| **Coty** | World’s largest pure‑fragrance house and a fast‑growing “beauty‑tech” player after buying Kylie Cosmetics and expanding into professional hair‑care (Wella, OPI). |
| **Amorepacific** | Korea’s leading beauty group; known for innovative “K‑beauty” formulations and a strong e‑commerce presence. |
| **Kao** | Combines cosmetics with household and pharma; its skin‑care brands (Biore, Curél) dominate the Japanese market and are expanding globally. |
| **Johnson & Johnson** | Though a health‑care conglomerate, its consumer‑health beauty brands (Neutrogena, Aveeno) are among the most trusted worldwide. |

### Quick reference timeline (founding years)

- **1837 – Procter & Gamble** (USA)  
- **1886 – Johnson & Johnson** (USA)  
- **1887 – Kao** (Japan)  
- **1872 – Shiseido** (Japan)  
- **1885 – Lever Brothers** (origin of Unilever)  
- **1904 – Coty** (USA)  
- **1909 – L’Oréal** (France)  
- **1930 – Unilever** (merger of Lever Brothers & Margarine Union)  
- **1945 – Amorepacific** (South Korea)  
- **1946 – Estée Lauder** (USA)  
- **1987 – LVMH** (France)  

These dates mark the foundation of the parent corporations; many of the famous consumer‑facing brands (e.g., Maybelline 1909, Clinique 1968, Dior 1947) were launched later as part of the same groups.

### Why these companies rank at the top
| Company | What makes it a “cosmetics giant” |
|---|---|
| **L’Oréal** | By far the world’s biggest pure‑beauty group; > 30 global brands, presence in > 150 countries, strong R&D (500 + patents a year) and aggressive M&A (e.g., IT Cosmetics, Aesop). |
| **Unilever** | Beauty & personal‑care is its second‑largest division after Foods; portfolio combines mass‑market (Dove, Sunsilk) and premium (Guerlain, Yves Saint Laurent) after the 2023 acquisition of Love Beauty and Planet. |
| **Estée Lauder** | Focused exclusively on prestige cosmetics; high‑margin luxury positioning and a fast‑growing “skin‑care‑first” strategy. |
| **Procter & Gamble** | Its Beauty & Grooming segment (hair‑care, skin‑care, men’s grooming) drives the fastest growth in the overall P&G business. |
| **LVMH** | Luxury conglomerate; its Perfumes & Cosmetics division (Dior, Guerlain, Fenty) accounts for > 30 % of group profit despite a smaller headcount. |
| **Shiseido** | Oldest Asian beauty house; strong in both mass (Shiseido, Anessa) and premium (Clé de Peau) markets, plus a growing digital‑beauty portfolio. |
| **Coty** | World’s largest pure‑fragrance house and a fast‑growing “beauty‑tech” player after buying Kylie Cosmetics and expanding into professional hair‑care (Wella, OPI). |
| **Amorepacific** | Korea’s leading beauty group; known for innovative “K‑beauty” formulations and a strong e‑commerce presence. |
| **Kao** | Combines cosmetics with household and pharma; its skin‑care brands (Biore, Curél) dominate the Japanese market and are expanding globally. |
| **Johnson & Johnson** | Though a health‑care conglomerate, its consumer‑health beauty brands (Neutrogena, Aveeno) are among the most trusted worldwide. |

### Quick reference timeline (founding years)

- **1837 – Procter & Gamble** (USA)  
- **1886 – Johnson & Johnson** (USA)  
- **1887 – Kao** (Japan)  
- **1872 – Shiseido** (Japan)  
- **1885 – Lever Brothers** (origin of Unilever)  
- **1904 – Coty** (USA)  
- **1909 – L’Oréal** (France)  
- **1930 – Unilever** (merger of Lever Brothers & Margarine Union)  
- **1945 – Amorepacific** (South Korea)  
- **1946 – Estée Lauder** (USA)  
- **1987 – LVMH** (France)  

These dates mark the foundation of the parent corporations; many of the famous consumer‑facing brands (e.g., Maybelline 1909, Clinique 1968, Dior 1947) were launched later as part of the same groups.
